items: Z-drugs: Complex Sleep Behaviors (sleepwalking, sleep-eating, sleep-driving) Black Box warning and amnesia (DSM p.453, p.472, Dulcan p.483)
Trazodone: Priapism (α1 blockade) emergency if erection > 4 hours, orthostatic hypotension, carryover sedation (Dulcan p.482, p.751)
Trazodone + SSRI interaction in youth: 6x lower response, 3x higher self-harm risk (Dulcan p.751)
Mirtazapine: Weight gain, increased appetite, sedation (Dulcan p.482)
Clonidine: Rebound hypertension on abrupt stop, bradycardia, hypotension (Dulcan p.482, StahlKids p.143)
Diphenhydramine: Anticholinergic toxicity (M1 blockade), paradoxical excitation, rapid tolerance (Dulcan p.482, StahlNeuro p.425)
DORAs: Daytime somnolence, abnormal dreams, contraindicated in Narcolepsy (StahlNeuro p.429, p.434)
key_numbers: 4 hours: Priapism emergency cutoff time for Trazodone (Dulcan p.751)
6x lower SSRI response when adding Trazodone in resistant depression (Dulcan p.751)
3x higher self-harm risk when adding Trazodone to SSRI (Dulcan p.751)

items: Clonidine: Baseline and post-titration blood pressure and heart rate monitoring; avoid abrupt stop (StahlKids p.142-143)
Trazodone: Mandatory patient/parent education on priapism risk and ER emergency protocol for erections > 4h (Dulcan p.751, StahlKids p.453)
Mirtazapine: Baseline and monthly weight, BMI, and metabolic profile monitoring (Dulcan p.482, StahlKids p.2)
Z-drugs: Active screening for complex sleep behaviors; immediate discontinuation if present (DSM p.472, Dulcan p.483)
General: Re-evaluate sleep hygiene and behavioral interventions at every follow-up (Dulcan p.480, p.494)
key_numbers: 4 hours: ER emergency threshold for priapism on Trazodone (Dulcan p.751)
3-4 months: Serum ferritin monitoring interval for RLS iron therapy (Dulcan p.484)

items: Melatonin: 0.3-6.0 mg (up to 10 mg in adolescents) given 30-60 min before bedtime, or 0.5 mg 3-5 hours before DLMO for phase shift (Dulcan p.482, p.491, StahlKids p.2)
Low-dose Trazodone: 12.5-100 mg in children, 50-150 mg in adolescents at bedtime (StahlKids p.455)
Mirtazapine: 7.5-15 mg at bedtime for insomnia with decreased appetite (Dulcan p.482, StahlKids p.127)
Clonidine IR: 0.025-0.05 mg initial, max 0.1-0.3 mg at bedtime for ADHD insomnia (Dulcan p.482, StahlKids p.141)
Zolpidem: 5-10 mg in adults (5 mg in women/elderly); 0.25 mg/kg failed in pediatric ADHD trials (Dulcan p.483, StahlNeuro p.422)
Low-dose Doxepin: 1-6 mg at bedtime for WASO/sleep maintenance in adults (DSM p.472, StahlNeuro p.425)

high_yield: Zero FDA-approved hypnotics exist for pediatric insomnia; all pediatric sleep prescriptions are off-label (Dulcan p.480, StahlKids p.319)
Zolpidem and Eszopiclone failed randomized controlled trials in pediatric ADHD insomnia (Blumer 2009, Zammit 2012) (Dulcan p.483)
Zolpidem selectively binds GABA-A α1 subunit (sedation only), unlike Benzodiazepines and Eszopiclone which bind α1, α2, α3, α5 (StahlNeuro p.422-423, Syllabus p.50)
Z-drugs carry a Black Box Warning for Complex Sleep Behaviors (sleepwalking, sleep-eating, sleep-driving) with complete amnesia (DSM p.453, p.472, Dulcan p.483)
DORAs block orexin OX1R/OX2R receptors to reduce arousal without GABAergic dependence, rebound, or tolerance, but are contraindicated in Narcolepsy (DSM p.472, StahlNeuro p.423, p.429)
Melatonin is first-line evidence-based therapy in pediatric ID (34 min SOL reduction, 50 min TST increase) and ASD (Dulcan p.172, p.482, p.493)
Low-dose Trazodone (25-100 mg) increases Slow-Wave Sleep via 5-HT2A antagonism, but carries α1-mediated Priapism emergency risk (>4h) (Dulcan p.482, p.751, StahlKids p.453)
Low-dose Doxepin (1-6 mg) is a selective H1 antagonist for sleep maintenance without M1 anticholinergic side effects or weight gain (DSM p.472, StahlNeuro p.425-426)
